question: For the Council of the District of Columbia: (1) the usual party composition (Democrats, independents, the two at-large seats that D.C. Code reserves from the majority party, Statehood Green, Republicans) and how it has changed since 2000; (2) the typical age and years of service of members; (3) which seats are elected in which years (the four-year staggered terms of wards 1, 2, 4, 6 and 8 versus 3, 5 and 7, the at-large seats and the Chairman); (4) the qualifications for a Council seat (age, residency, registration, ward residency).
requestedBy: Codex's overnight dispatch (item 12d, D.C. Council ordinances missing), relayed by the coordinator at 3:34 a.m. Eastern on September 23, 2026; filed by the D.C. Council thread

sourcesChecked.source: D.C. Code §§ 1-204.04, 1-204.12 and 1-206.02, locked in data/source/municipal-governance/raw from the Council's law-xml-codified repository
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: § 1-204.01 (already locked) fixes thirteen members, the Chairman and four at large and one per ward; it does not give party, age, term staggering or qualifications.

terms.notice: 17 USC105 government works; statistics/facts only, not third-party content or logos.

title: Who sits on the D.C. Council at a game's start: party, age, tenure and which seat is up
usableAnswer: A party table, an age and tenure summary, the seat-by-year election schedule, and the qualifications, each with its source.
whyItMatters: A life started in the District now seats all thirteen members (src/simulation/nationwide-world/district-of-columbia-council-opening.ts). Their ages are drawn from 25 to 80, nobody has a party because the save's political conditions carry no share for the District, and a Council race names no ward or at-large seat, so a player who wins it while every seat is filled is not seated at all. The first two are placeholders; the third waits on knowing which seats are up in which year.

findings.finding: Exact federal/DC rules and locked primary state facts are supplied where verified. Remaining state/local structure and age/tenure distributions are explicitly unresolved. Neither a legal age minimum nor town population implies a uniform age window or council size. No real-person names collected.
